look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: Find the mallow-like flower and, most importantly, a mature flattened disk-shaped fruit (schizocarp). Count the wedge-shaped segments (mericarps) and inspect their projecting points; do not identify this plant from a purple leaf blotch or flower color alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual herb with spreading to upright branching stems; habit varies with disturbance and moisture.

key_traits.label: Leaves attachment
key_traits.text: Alternate, petiolate leaves; lower leaves may be broader or lobed and upper leaves narrower. Variable purple marks are not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Flower reproductive
key_traits.text: Solitary five-petaled, mallow-type flowers with many stamens united into a central column; check calyx and flower attachment.

key_traits.label: Fruit seed
key_traits.text: Flattened circular schizocarp breaks into approximately 10–19 wedge-shaped mericarps. Mature mericarp tips/spines are more decisive than flower color.

key_traits.label: Stem bud
key_traits.text: Inspect leaf axils for flower and fruit stalks; note hairiness and alternate nodes.
